posts.text: When kids use AI to complete schoolwork, they're not offloading skills they already have—they're skipping the process of developing them. Rebecca Winthrop makes the case for treating this as "cognitive stunting" and what it means for policy. brook.gs/4f7aQ4w

Has the U.S. lost the Iran war? Robert Kagan, Michael O'Hanlon, and Melanie Sisson assess the state of the conflict, Iran's control of the Strait of Hormuz, and the options still available to Washington on the latest Current podcast episode. brook.gs/4tKmzth

Beijing and Washington walked away from the Trump-Xi summit reading very different scorecards. Ryan Hass, Patricia Kim, Kyle Chan, and Jon Czin break down what China's leadership actually heard—and what it means for the relationship going forward. brook.gs/4v3xMXc

Up to 237,000 housing units could be built on underutilized postal sites—including ~117,000 in areas with the most acute supply shortages. Aaron Shroyer, Ben McAdams, and Glen Nuckolls on how USPS could turn real estate into a revenue asset while helping solve the housing crisis. brook.gs/4v9lDA1

Ahead of Africa Day, @LandrySigne talks with @AmbMukantabana, ambassador of Rwanda to the U.S. and dean of the African Diplomatic Corps, to discuss how African governments are coordinating their diplomatic efforts in response to new priorities and opportunities. Listen to the new Foresight Africa episode 🎧 brookings.edu/articles/afric…

Trump's second-term tariffs are historic in scale—but their U.S. economic impact has been more muted than expected. For the BPEA podcast, Pablo Fajgelbaum and Amit Khandelwal dig into what they've accomplished, where costs have fallen, and what's ahead. brook.gs/49JD2XA

President Trump's March order targets mail-in and absentee voting—raising legal questions about who actually has authority over federal elections. Samara Angel and Jonathan Katz break down the risks of executive overreach, implementation hurdles, and potential voter disenfranchisement. brook.gs/3RhDyG4

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz is one of the biggest energy disruptions in decades—and its full economic ripple effects are still unfolding. Adie Tomer and Samantha Gross break down what it means for American consumers and U.S. energy security 🎙️ brook.gs/4nxcsXt

New research reveals that more than 145,000 U.S. citizen children have been separated from their parents under the administration's immigration crackdown. Tara Watson and co-authors break down what the data show—and what policymakers must address. brook.gs/4dBo72X

Kevin Warsh is about to inherit a Federal Reserve that earns a B+ on communications—but where 75% of Fed watchers rate the threat to independence as a 4 or 5 out of 5. Sarah Ahmad and @davidmwessel survey what markets and academics think heading into the leadership transition. brook.gs/4udVcJ9

The U.S. and China share a national security interest in preventing AI-enabled attacks from nonstate actors—even as they compete for AI dominance. @kyleichan and @ryanl_hass make the case for practical cooperation as the Trump-Xi summit gets underway. brook.gs/42kiNMb

Congressional primaries in both parties are functioning as early referendums on intraparty power in 2026. Elaine Kamarck breaks down what's happened so far—and which May races will tell us the most. brook.gs/48YLW3e

What does Beijing really want from the war in Iran, and what does Washington want from China? Jon Czin, Ryan Hass, Suzanne Maloney, and Mara Karlin break down the U.S.-China-Iran triangle on the latest Beijing Brief: brook.gs/4nk60Ty

Video
What's at stake when Trump meets Xi in Beijing on May 14-15? Nine experts from across Brookings weigh in on AI governance, Taiwan, fentanyl, energy, and more. brook.gs/4uyat7D

What steps can the U.S. take to sharpen its strategic advantages over China? Join us next Monday, May 11 at 4:00 PM for a conversation with @SenatorShaheen and @SenThomTillis on Congressional policy priorities in the US-China competition. brook.gs/4wfwpG0

About 1 in 5 college students receives state financial aid, but do "free college" programs actually improve outcomes? Katharine Meyer and Isabel McMullen examine which design and support features make state promise programs work. brook.gs/49feEgc
